title: Microrelease operator handbook for LLM routing
content:
Purpose and scope:
This document is a working operator handbook aimed at the oncall/operator and product steward for microreleases that change inference routing (model selection, region routing, or tier fallbacks). Focus: coordinated canaries and A/B slices where routing decisions, not model code, are the primary change.

Goals:
- Keep customer-facing latency and error-rate impact < defined thresholds during exposure.
- Provide a compact checklist for rapid rollback and post-mortem starting artifacts.
- Clarify cross-functional responsibilities (product, infra, SRE, observability, legal for regulated customers).

When to use this playbook:
- Introducing new routing policy (cost-driven vs latency-driven)
- Adding a routing tier (e.g., fallback to quantized model under load)
- Multi-model blends (ensemble/reranker routing changes)
- Region routing or dual-control tests (EU->us-east redirect experiments)

High-level roles and primary responsibilities:
- Release Steward (product): owns hypothesis, target KPI, and customer impact assessment.
- Operator (infra/SRE): executes activation & rollback, monitors infra signals.
- Observability Lead: defines signal set, sets temporary dashboards/alerts.
- Safety Steward (research/QA): defines QA prompt set and human review escalation path.
- Comms Lead (customer-success): prepares templated comms for impacted customers.

Pre-release checklist (must be green before any traffic is routed):
1) Hypothesis and success criteria documented (one paragraph) + experiment key (Jira).
2) Risk matrix completed for high-risk slices (payment, legal, admin flows).
3) Canary slices identified (cohort size, sampling method, time window). Avoid overlapping cohorts with existing experiments.
4) Dedicated dashboards created: prefix latency hist, per-slice error-rate, model mismatch ratio, cost per 1k tokens.
5) Synthetic traffic replay to simulate worst-case KV cache miss and long-context requests.
6) Rollback plan and automated toggle prepared in the console; rollback < 3 clicks or single API call.
7) Oncall and cross-functional rotation scheduled for the rollout window.
8) If private deployments involved, secure a point contact and confirm KMS access for metrics.

Traffic partitioning recommendations:
- Start small: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% with 30–60 minute observation windows (shorter windows for low-latency critical flows).
- Prefer household or account-based splits over IP splits to reduce sample contamination when sessions persist.
- For model routing policy changes (cost vs quality), weight slices by traffic intensity and feature type.
- Use deterministic sample keys where possible so retries remain consistent to the same variant.

Signals to watch (primary + secondary):
Primary (auto-alert rules):
- 99th percentile token latency (per-route) – alert if > baseline + 25% or > SLA threshold.
- Per-route model-inference error rate (exceptions, timeouts) – alert if > baseline + 5ppt.
- Model mismatch ratio (new vs control outputs flagged as invalid) – alert if trend upwards.
- Cost per request (token-based spend estimate) – alert for > 30% delta.

Secondary (human review cadence):
- Semantic quality regressions on the safety prompt set (sample size 200 per wave).
- Customer-reported issues via CS tags (tag traffic sample id in tickets).
- Reranker/LLM hallucination markers: hallucination score drift on benchmark prompts.

Fast rollback decision criteria (operator):
- Any primary alert fires twice within 15 minutes.
- One P1 customer report tied to the new routing variant and reproducible.
- Latency tail crossing SLA for more than one minute for >5% of affected requests.

Rollback steps (operator runbook):
1) Pause new exposures: toggle the experiment to 0% in console (API: POST /rollouts/{id}/pause).
2) Re-route to control: set routing policy to pinned control model for affected paths (CLI: rwdctl route set --policy pinned-control).
3) Confirm traffic shift: check per-route traffic counters and session cookie mapping (target 95% traffic on control within 60s).
4) Post-rollback validate: run smoke checks (10 requests across critical flows) and validate KV cache warmup.
5) Stakeholder notify: send rollback announcement to #release-watch and CS with impact note.

Staged validation templates (copy and adapt):
- 1% exposure: validate no alerts in 30 minutes; take 20 human QA checks on safety set.
- 5% exposure: validate latency and error-rate hold for 1 hour; run automated regression suite.
- 20% exposure: validate cost model and observe user-facing metrics for 2 hours.
- Full exposure: final 6-hour observation and handover to steady-state owner.

Human-in-the-loop escalation path:
- If safety steward flags > 2 failing prompts in any wave, trigger immediate rollback and start a dedicated triage thread.
- Provide a pre-made ticket template that includes sample request/response, timestamps, routing metadata, and region.

Edge-case tactics and mitigation notes:
- Cold-KV storms: limit sampling to short-session cohorts and avoid launching during cache warmup windows.
- Burst traffic: enable autoscaling override to minimum safe headroom before expansion.
- Quantization regression: if output diversity drops, route only low-risk endpoints to quantized variants.

Observability checklist (must be created pre-launch):
- Temporary dashboard with: per-cohort throughput, per-cohort p50/p95/p99 latency, model-fallback-rate, token-cost burn rate, top error types.
- Alerts: primary signal thresholds with runbook links.
- Logging: include routing decision id, model-version, policy-reason in every request log.

Post-release artifacts to produce within 48 hours:
- Brief: 1-page slip: what happened, metrics snapshot, decision log (time, actor, action).
- Incident ticket if any P1/P0 opened + action items.
- Cost delta report (first 24h vs baseline).
- QA sample set with annotations (human labels).

Retrospective template (questions):
- Did the hypothesis match measurement?
- Which signals were most predictive of user impact?
- Were the cohort splits contaminated?
- What ops automation could have reduced time-to-rollback?
- Next steps and who owns them.

Open questions / TBDs (working):
- How should we version routing policies to allow backfill analysis (short-term: embed policy id in logs; long-term: policy store).
- What is the canonical customer-visible KPI for hybrid routing changes (latency vs semantic quality tradeoff)?
- Decide standard sampling cadence for long-lived experiments (>7 days) to avoid drift.

Quick-reference commands (examples for operator):
- Pause rollout: curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://console.redwood.ai/api/rollouts/{id}/pause
- Force route control: rwdctl route set --path /search --policy pinned-control --model redwood-001
- Dump recent routing decisions (last 5 minutes): rwdctl logs query --filter "route_decision:true" --window 5m

Notes to self / reminders:
- Keep the safety prompt set refreshed monthly; tag prompts with the routing experiment id.
- Call out private deployment customers explicitly in the runbook and set up a pre-notify workflow.
- This doc is an operator-facing concise handbook; push longer playbook to Confluence once stable.

End of doc — quick checklist summary (for printing):
- Hypothesis & success criteria ✅
- Cohorts defined & non-overlapping ✅
- Dashboards & alerts ✅
- Synthetic replay ✅
- Rollback toggles ✅
- Oncall scheduled ✅
- Safety steward sign-off ✅

(If you are the operator executing this, add timestamp and initial to the top of the experiment ticket after start.)
